what_happened: Scene layout 6 (speckled granite counter, wood floor, toaster oven on the counter; robot right of the dishwasher), white/pink cup_5 and a shallow dark-red wooden bowl_9 lying near the counter's front edge. Stage 0: cup grasped 148-157 (lift 0.095), released on the slid-out rack at 350 (0.03 m, upright); stage 0 complete 367 (normal). Stage 1: the gripper came down on the near rim of the flat bowl (touch 494-505, close 499 on the bowl: width 0.021, no lift) and, with the fingers on the rim, dragged it toward the dishwasher 512-529 (packet 'hold' with lift 0.0). At ~528-536 the bowl slid over the counter's front edge, clipped the rack (at_target for one step, 533) and fell to the floor beside the open door (drop 0.878 m; wrist 536-560 shows it on the floor right of the door; end z 0.019, 0.32 m from the dishwasher). The policy did not go after it: from ~560 it went to the dishwasher, pushed the rack in and closed the door (closedness 0.16@768, 0.38@800, 1.00@816; done 814-1200), then stayed at the control panel to the end.
causal_chain: fingers closed on the rim of the flat bowl at 499 without a grip -> bowl dragged along the counter and off its edge (528-536) -> bowl on the floor (0.88 m drop) -> policy skipped to the door and closed it at 814 with only the cup inside -> stage 1 never completes
self_recovery: none: no attempt to pick the bowl up from the floor; the policy moved straight on to closing the door.
official_criterion_notes: Stage 1 held for one step (533) while the falling bowl brushed the rack; first_complete_step 533 is a false positive of the rack-contact test (the bowl was in free fall). Door fixture done 814-1200 although stage 1 never held.

packet_facts: close 499 on dish1, not lifted; dish1 hold 512-529 lift 0.0 drop 0.878; end z 0.019

uncertain_about: Whether the drag was an attempted slide-off-the-edge grasp strategy or the fingers catching the rim while closing; the result is the same.
